BERUT-NATURE-2012.citation: A. Berut et al., Experimental verification of Landauer's principle linking information and thermodynamics, Nature 483, 187-189 (2012)
registered_rows: A classical one-bit memory was implemented by one colloidal particle in a modulated double-well potential.
Erasing the memory produced a finite mean dissipated heat.
The mean dissipated heat saturated at the Landauer bound in the limit of long erasure cycles.
The paper reports an experimental information-thermodynamics correspondence and an irreversible-computation limit.
scope_rows: The reported saturation is a long-cycle limiting mean, not a claim that every individual finite-time erasure has identical heat.
The experiment tests a generic model of a one-bit memory; it does not identify an SFT native half-One carrier with a dimensional joule value.

PIECHOCINSKA-PRA-2000.citation: B. Piechocinska, Information erasure, Physical Review A 61, 062314 (2000)
registered_rows: Erasure is a reset from two distinguishable bit states to one possible state.
For a symmetric equiprobable bit in contact with a thermal reservoir, average work and dissipated heat are bounded below by k_B T ln 2.
The microscopic treatment covers classical continuous, classical discrete and quantum cases.
The bound is explicitly an ensemble-average statement.
scope_rows: The derivation assumes contact with a thermal reservoir.
For a non-equiprobable initial distribution the lower bound depends on that distribution.
The conventional logarithm is retained only as an external dimensional translation and never enters the SFT proof scalar domain.
